title: What Space Actually Does to Your Body
hook: Right now, atmospheric pressure is keeping the water inside your body from boiling.
script: Right now, atmospheric pressure is keeping the water inside your body from boiling. If an airlock blew open, would your body pop like a balloon? Your tough collagen skin actually stretches instead of bursting. So why do you still pass out in only 15 seconds? In a vacuum, your lungs violently reverse, stripping oxygen backward out of your blood. Can a human survive ebullism when fluids boil at normal body temperature? In 1965, an exposed NASA technician felt his saliva boil and made a full recovery. Since animals survive two minutes flatlined, should vacuum decompression be treated as a rescue window or certain death?

captions: If you were exposed to space without a suit, is it a brief rescue window or instant death? Most sci-fi gets this backwards.
Hollywood lied about exploding bodies in a vacuum. Here is what human physiology actually does.
The 15-second rule of space decompression and why your own blood betrays you first.
